## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Cline #14378 max-tokens recovery - HIGH PRIORITY (core)

- **What**: Cline PR #14378 "fix(agents,llms): recover from max-tokens turns and scale the default output budget" merged 2026-09-22 implemented max-tokens recovery (agent turns ending at output-token limit without usable tool call were top crash per Cline telemetry; recovery allows up to MAX_TOKENS_RECOVERY_LIMIT=3 consecutive cut-offs, appending conciseness nudge "one small step at a time, large outputs in chunks" after each; counter resets on any turn producing a tool call so single over-long response recovers while repeated overflow ends run; also scales default per-request output cap from flat 32k to 30% of model's advertised output budget DEFAULT_GATEWAY_MAX_OUTPUT_FRACTION, taking max of fraction and flat default so small-budget models not undercut; reasoning budget still lifts cap, model/context limits still clamp). This is output-budget resilience (graceful recovery from max-tokens cutoff, turn-level retry with conciseness steering, adaptive default output cap).

- **Why**: Alexi has no max-tokens recovery (orchestrator in src/core/orchestrator.ts, agenticChat.ts handle tool loop retries for transient errors but not for output-limit cutoffs; a max-tokens turn = run failure). Reasoning models (Claude Opus 4.x with extended thinking, o1/o3) and large tool payloads regularly hit output limits. Cline's recovery pattern (allow up to 3 consecutive cutoffs with conciseness nudge, reset counter on successful tool call) is directly portable to Alexi. Implementation path: detect max-tokens finish_reason in provider response (src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts, check finish_reason === 'max_tokens'), maintain cutoff counter in agenticChat loop state, append conciseness system message after cutoff, retry turn (same logic as transient-error retry but with different reason), reset counter on tool call, fail run after 3 consecutive cutoffs.

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14378 (Cline max-tokens recovery, merged 2026-09-22), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/agenticChat.ts (Alexi agentic loop, no max-tokens recovery), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/orchestrator.ts (orchestrator, no cutoff detection)

- **Category**: core (agenticChat loop + orchestrator cutoff detection)

- **Size**: MEDIUM (~6-8h). Add finish_reason check in provider response handlers (src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts, detect 'max_tokens' finish_reason from SAP AI Core / Anthropic / OpenAI responses), add cutoff counter to agenticChat loop state (MAX_TOKENS_RECOVERY_LIMIT=3), append conciseness system message after cutoff ("Be concise. Provide one small step at a time. Large outputs should be chunked."), retry turn (reuse existing retry infrastructure), reset counter on successful tool call, fail run with clear message after 3 consecutive cutoffs, add adaptive default output cap (30% of model's advertised output budget from modelCatalog, max with flat 32k default), write tests (single cutoff recovers, 3 consecutive cutoffs fail, counter reset on tool call, adaptive cap calculation).

#### 2. Kilocode #14445 agent goal tool - HIGH PRIORITY (tool + core)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14445 "feat(goal): let the agent start or resume a session goal" merged 2026-09-22 implemented agent-facing goal tool (agent can start or resume a session goal itself via tool call; unlike /goal command which cancels current turn, goal tool arms goal without cancelling so goal loop continues after turn finishes; tool requests goal permission, hidden while goal already active, rejects delegated subagent sessions; shares continuation loop + admission checks + run-target resolution with /goal command; goal loop is multi-turn continuation with explicit target, arms after current turn completes). This is autonomous goal management (agent can self-initiate multi-turn goals, permission-gated, non-interrupting goal arming).

- **Why**: Alexi has no goal management mechanism (CLI `alexi chat` is one-shot prompt → response or interactive REPL with prompt loop in src/cli/interactive.ts; no persistent multi-turn goal tracking, no continuation state across prompts, no agent-initiated goals). Kilocode's goal tool lets the agent say "I will now work toward X across multiple turns" and persist that intent, resuming the goal after intermediate tool calls / user prompts. Useful for complex multi-step tasks (implement feature → write tests → verify → commit) where agent wants explicit continuation signal beyond single-turn tool loop. Implementation path: add goal tool definition (src/tool/tools/goal.ts, schema with goal description + optional target, requests new 'goal' permission), add goal state to session metadata (src/core/sessionManager.ts, Session.metadata.goal: { description: string, target?: string, armed: boolean }), implement goal loop (after tool execution / user response, check if goal armed and continue turn automatically with goal context injected as system message), add /goal CLI command (src/cli/commands/goal.ts, UI for setting goal interactively), add permission check (src/permission/, goal permission required for tool call).

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14445 (Kilocode goal tool, merged 2026-09-22), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/interactive.ts (Alexi REPL, no goal state), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/sessionManager.ts (session state, no goal field)

- **Category**: tool + core (goal tool definition + session goal state + continuation loop)

- **Size**: LARGE (~16-20h). Add goal tool (src/tool/tools/goal.ts with Zod schema, registers in src/tool/registry.ts), extend session metadata (Session.metadata.goal: { description: string, target?: string, armed: boolean, createdAt: number }), implement goal arming (tool handler sets goal.armed=true, does not cancel current turn), implement goal continuation loop (after agenticChat completes turn, check session.metadata.goal.armed, inject goal context as system message "Continue working toward goal: <description>", call orchestrator again with goal context), add goal permission (src/permission/types.ts, goal permission check in tool handler), add /goal CLI command (src/cli/commands/goal.ts, interactive goal setting + status + clear), add goal status display in TUI (src/cli/tui/, show active goal in header), write tests (goal arming, continuation loop, permission check, goal clear, multi-turn goal execution).

#### 4. Kilocode #14448 provider auth allowlist - LOW PRIORITY (providers)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14448 "fix(cli): skip providers excluded by enabled_providers before auth loaders" merged 2026-09-22 fixed provider auth loop crash (when enabled_providers excluded kilo while Kilo login was stored, plugin auth loader still ran for kilo and passed missing catalog entry to toPublicInfo, throwing HTTP 500 for /provider and /config/providers; fix skips providers not allowed by enabled_providers or disabled_providers before auth loader runs, guards against missing catalog entry). This is provider initialization robustness (auth loader gating by allow/deny lists).

- **Why**: Alexi has provider gating (src/providers/auth.ts, enabled_providers / disabled_providers config via src/config/userConfig.ts), but may run auth loaders for excluded providers before checking if they are enabled (check src/providers/auth.ts loadProviderAuthStates or similar initialization). Kilocode's fix gates auth loader execution by allow/deny list *before* expensive auth state loads / token refresh / catalog lookups. Low priority (optimization / crash prevention for edge case: excluded provider with stale stored auth). Implementation path: audit provider initialization (src/providers/auth.ts or src/providers/index.ts, check if getProviderForModel / getAvailableModels filters providers before or after auth loader runs), move enabled_providers / disabled_providers check to earliest point (before auth loader invocation), add guard for missing catalog entry (if provider not in catalog, skip gracefully), write test (excluded provider with stale auth does not crash).

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14448 (Kilocode provider auth allowlist, merged 2026-09-22), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/auth.ts (Alexi provider auth), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/config/userConfig.ts (enabled_providers config)

- **Category**: provider (auth initialization gating)

- **Size**: SMALL (~1-2h). Audit provider initialization order (src/providers/auth.ts loadProviderAuthStates or similar, check if enabled_providers / disabled_providers checked before or after auth loaders run), move filter check to earliest point (before auth loader invocation in loadProviderAuthStates or equivalent), add guard for missing catalog entry (if provider not in modelCatalog, skip auth loader gracefully with warning), write test (excluded provider with stale auth does not crash, missing catalog entry handled gracefully).

#### 5. Kilocode #14361 shell output highlighting - LOW PRIORITY (tui)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14361 "fix(ui): highlight streaming shell output incrementally" merged 2026-09-22 optimized TUI shell output rendering (streaming shell output now syntax-highlighted incrementally during render instead of re-highlighting entire output on every chunk; removed stale tail with single Range DOM operation instead of loop; improved visual regression baselines). This is TUI performance optimization (incremental syntax highlighting for streaming shell output).

- **Why**: Alexi has Ink-based TUI (src/cli/tui/) with streaming shell output display (bash tool streams output to TUI via src/tool/tools/bash-streaming.ts). Kilocode's optimization (incremental highlighting during streaming) is TUI-specific performance win for long shell outputs. Low priority (Alexi TUI may already batch updates efficiently via Ink's reconciliation; profile before implementing). Implementation path: audit shell output rendering (src/cli/tui/, check if bash streaming output is syntax-highlighted and whether highlighting re-runs on every chunk), implement incremental highlighting (track last-highlighted line, only highlight new lines on chunk arrival), profile TUI performance with large shell outputs (e.g. npm install, find /, git log --all), implement if measurable regression found.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14361 (Kilocode shell highlighting, merged 2026-09-22), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/bash-streaming.ts (Alexi bash streaming), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/tui/ (TUI rendering)

- **Category**: tui (shell output rendering performance)

- **Size**: SMALL (~2-3h). Profile Alexi TUI shell output rendering (src/cli/tui/, measure render time for large bash outputs), audit existing highlighting (check if cli-highlight or similar used, whether re-applied on every chunk), implement incremental highlighting if profiling shows regression (track last-highlighted line offset, only highlight new lines), write test (incremental highlighting does not re-process entire output on chunk).
